approval.cost: No fee or price was stated on the pages read
approval.trigger: App Review is required for real users: 'If your app will be used by anyone without a Role on the app or a role in a Business that has claimed the app, it must first undergo App Review'; if only users with a role on the app itself use it, App Review is not required. The pre-approval cap is role-based: approved permissions 'can be requested from any app user, but unapproved permissions can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app'; approved features are active for all users, unapproved only for role holders. Two permissions are exempt: the Web docs state public_profile and email 'do not require app review and are automatically granted'. The review has two components that both must pass: app verification (reviewers test that the app works, follows described use cases, and meets the UX quality bar; you must provide a version of the app and test instructions) and permissions review (reviewers check you requested only necessary permissions/features). 'If Meta cannot access/test the app, your entire submission will be rejected'; if a specific permission/feature cannot be tested, that item will not be approved. Advanced Access adds prerequisites: starting 'on or after June 12th, 2023', apps requiring advanced level access must complete business verification and data handling questions, and Business Verification (from 2023) must be completed to finish review. App Settings (icon, privacy policy URL, category, business email, platforms) is necessary to submit.
approval.wait: Not stated (no review duration or turnaround time was stated on the readable App Review pages; the App Review FAQs page rendered with an empty article body in the reading session, so no timeline could be verified from it)

blockers.detail: Approved permissions 'can be requested from any app user, but unapproved permissions can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app'. Until App Review passes, your real users literally cannot grant the permissions your app needs (beyond public_profile and email).
blockers.howToClear: Submit for App Review with a testable app version and test instructions before onboarding real users.
blockers.title: Unapproved permissions are role-holders-only

blockers.detail: If an app 'does not use a permission for 90 days, that permission may expire', even if it was approved through app review. Users may also grant only a subset of requested permissions and may revoke at any time, so granted_scopes must be checked per user.
blockers.howToClear: Exercise every approved permission within each 90-day window and verify granted permissions via /me/permissions at connect time.
blockers.title: Permissions expire from disuse

blockers.detail: Short-lived user tokens live about one to two hours. Long-lived tokens (about 60 days) come from exchanging a short-lived token, and the SDKs refresh them only 'if the person used the app within the last 90 days', 'refreshed once per day': a dormant user's token dies even though nothing was revoked.
blockers.howToClear: Exchange for long-lived tokens immediately and design a re-login path for dormant users.
blockers.title: Token lifetimes and the 90-day activity window

alternatives: App access token (App ID + App Secret, grant_type=client_credentials; server-side only; for app-level operations, not user data)
Page access token (unique to each Page/admin/app, obtained via {user-id}/accounts; long-lived Page tokens 'do not have an expiration date' and only expire/are invalidated under certain conditions)

System User token (from Business Settings: Admin system users have full access to business portfolio assets by default; Employee system users are per-asset; the durable choice for business automation)

flavor.recommended: A Meta (Facebook) App with the Facebook Login product, using the manual OAuth flow (authorization code) for web servers
flavor.why: The object is a Facebook App (created in Meta for Developers with a Facebook Developer Account), identified by an App ID and App Secret. Adding the Facebook Login product enables user login. For web: in App Dashboard add Facebook Login, then Settings > Client OAuth Settings: enter Valid OAuth Redirect URIs, set 'Login with JavaScript SDK' to yes, and list Allowed Domains for the JavaScript SDK; only https pages are supported. The JS SDK flow runs FB.getLoginStatus (statuses connected / not_authorized / unknown; authResponse carries accessToken, expiresIn, reauthorize_required_in, signedRequest, userID), FB.login() (optionally {scope: 'public_profile,email'}), FB.logout(). The manual/server flow redirects to facebook.com/v26.0/dialog/oauth with client_id, redirect_uri, and state (CSRF); response_type can be code, token, 'code token', or granted_scopes; a code is exchanged server-to-server at GET graph.facebook.com/v26.0/oauth/access_token. Tokens are inspected with GET graph.facebook.com/debug_token and granted/declined permissions checked via /me/permissions. Permissions are strings passed via scope (e.g. pages_show_list, user_photos); public_profile is always required.

humanMust: Create a Facebook Developer Account and a Facebook App; add the Facebook Login product
Configure Client OAuth Settings (Valid OAuth Redirect URIs, JavaScript SDK login, Allowed Domains)
Complete App Settings (icon, privacy policy URL, category, business email, platforms) and, for advanced access, Business Verification and the data handling questions
Submit for App Review with a testable app version and test instructions
name: Facebook
nuances: Token types matter: User, App, Page, System User, and Client tokens are different objects with different lifetimes and custody rules; the App token uses the App Secret and must stay server-side.
Sample long-lived exchange response on the docs page shows expires_in 5183944 seconds (about 60 days). Long-lived Page tokens are the exception to expiry: they 'do not have an expiration date'.
Only https pages are supported for Facebook Login for Web, and the redirect URIs must be registered in Client OAuth Settings before the flow works.
prerequisites: An https site with registered redirect URIs
For advanced access: a business that can complete Business Verification

steps.detail: With a Facebook Developer Account, create an app and note the App ID. In the App Dashboard add Facebook Login; in Settings > Client OAuth Settings enter Valid OAuth Redirect URIs, set 'Login with JavaScript SDK' to yes, and list Allowed Domains for the JavaScript SDK (https only).
steps.title: Create the app; add Facebook Login; configure OAuth settings

steps.detail: Redirect the user to facebook.com/v26.0/dialog/oauth with client_id, redirect_uri, state, and response_type=code (or use the JS SDK's FB.login with a scope). Verify state on return; exchange the code server-to-server at GET graph.facebook.com/v26.0/oauth/access_token. Inspect tokens with debug_token and check granted/declined permissions via /me/permissions.
steps.title: Run the login flow; exchange the code

steps.detail: Exchange the short-lived token (about one to two hours) for a long-lived token (about 60 days). SDKs refresh long-lived tokens once per day if the person used the app within the last 90 days.
steps.title: Exchange for a long-lived token

steps.detail: Complete App Settings (icon, privacy policy URL, category, business email, platforms); for advanced access complete Business Verification and the data handling questions; submit with a testable app version and test instructions. Both app verification and permissions review must pass.
steps.title: Submit for App Review (and Business Verification for advanced access)

tagline: A Meta app with Facebook Login, where App Review is the real product gate: until it passes, only people with a role on your app can grant your permissions at all, and permissions you stop using for 90 days can expire even after approval.

time.active: ~20 min of app setup + ~2-3 hrs of flow code + review preparation
time.total: Unknown: App Review duration is not stated
